extracted.intended_audience: petitioners and patent owners (users of the AIA Review / PTAB filing system) who will file a rehearing request
extracted.subtask_description: Step-by-step procedural instructions for preparing and submitting a Rehearing Request under § 42.71 using the AIA Review Actions filing interface (including required metadata, upload, review, and docketing steps).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to request rehearing
rubrics_metrics.description: When the petitioner or patent owner disagrees with a board decision, they have an option to file a rehearing request. See § 42.71.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rehearing requests are the appropriate procedural vehicle when a party disagrees with a Board decision; cite § 42.71 for the governing rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to initiate a Rehearing Request in the filing system
rubrics_metrics.description: To initiate a Rehearing Request, Go to 'AIA Review Actions' menu and select 'File a Rehearing Request'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the AIA Review Actions workflow in the e-filing system (screenshots provided) to start the filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required metadata fields for the rehearing filing
rubrics_metrics.description: The party will enter the Filing Party, Rehearing Type, Type – Paper or Exhibit, Paper Type, Name - Document Name (or Exhibit Number) and Availability of the paper/exhibit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All listed metadata fields must be completed for the document to be properly recorded; ensure accuracy of each field before adding the document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing Party selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Enter the Filing Party – select Petitioner, Patent Owner, or Joint Request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the correct filing party to reflect who is submitting the rehearing request (Petitioner, Patent Owner, or Joint Request).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting the appropriate Rehearing Type
rubrics_metrics.description: Enter the Rehearing Request Type – this would be based upon what type of decision you are requesting be reheard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine which kind of Board decision is being challenged and select the matching rehearing type in the system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper Type must correspond to Rehearing Type
rubrics_metrics.description: Next select the Paper Type – which is the specific rehearing request related to the board decision. Note that the Rehearing Type and the Paper Type selection should match.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if the Rehearing Type is 'Order', then the paper type would be 'Rehearing Request – in re Board Order'. Ensure consistency between Rehearing Type and Paper Type to avoid misfiling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify whether the filing is a paper or an exhibit and name it
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify Type – Paper or Exhibit, and enter Name - Document Name (or Exhibit Number) and Availability of the paper/exhibit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correctly indicate whether the uploaded item is a filing paper or an exhibit, provide a clear document name or exhibit number, and mark its availability status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uploading the document(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Enter the paper and upload the document and click on the 'Add' button.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the upload control to attach the rehearing document (and any supporting documents/exhibits) then click 'Add' so the system records the file and associated metadata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review added documents and metadata before submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the document and metadata have been added, the document and metadata will appear in the table below. If satisfied with the results, click on the 'Submit' button.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify that the document(s) and metadata appear correctly in the table (correct party, type, name, availability) prior to submission; only submit when accurate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing or deleting documents prior to submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Go back to 'My Docket' and select the 'Rehearing' to see the request for rehearing document filed in the case: [Edit/Delete Documents].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Edit/Delete Documents functions available in the docket or the rehearing tab to modify or remove documents before final submission; screenshots show the controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viewing and downloading filed rehearing requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Click on the 'View Documents' button to see the request for rehearing filed and click on the 'Download' button to see the pdf document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After submission, use My Docket → Rehearing → View Documents → Download to retrieve the filed PDF and confirm the filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viewing rehearing request details
rubrics_metrics.description: Click on the 'View Details' button to see the detailed information about the Rehearing Request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use View Details to confirm metadata, filing party, rehearing type, paper type, and other recorded data for the rehearing request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessing started-but-not-submitted (draft) rehearing requests
rubrics_metrics.description: To view a Rehearing Request that has been started but not yet submitted, go to My Docket and click on the Rehearing tab and look for one that has a status of 'Initiated'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drafts are saved with status 'Initiated' in My Docket → Rehearing; locate and continue editing or submit from there.

rubrics_metrics.name: Starting/continuing a rehearing request from a Final Written Decision link
rubrics_metrics.description: Click on the 'Final Written Decision' link to access your already started Rehearing Request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The system provides a link from the Final Written Decision entry to access or continue a rehearing request associated with that decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document naming and view/property warnings
rubrics_metrics.description: The document will appear in the table below: [Document view properties warning]; Edit/Delete Documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay attention to any document view property warnings shown by the system (e.g., display or metadata warnings) and correct issues via edit/delete before submission.
